outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Controlling Diffusion Models
outline.description: This chapter sets the stage by defining the current state of text-to-image diffusion models and identifying the critical challenge of fine-tuning them for specific downstream tasks without degrading their pre-trained generative abilities. It introduces the two primary use cases explored in the research: Subject-Driven Generation and Controllable Generation.
subtopics: Overview of Large Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
The Fine-tuning Challenge: Balancing Adaptation vs. Catastrophic Forgetting
Desiderata for Effective Fine-tuning: Efficiency and Generalizability Preservation

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Theoretical Foundations of Neural Semantics
outline.description: Before introducing the proposed solution, this chapter builds the necessary theoretical background. It explores why neuron direction matters more than magnitude, defines Hyperspherical Energy, and explains the mathematical properties of orthogonal transformations that make them ideal for preserving semantic structure.
subtopics: Angular Information vs. Magnitude in Neural Representations
Hyperspherical Energy: Defining Pairwise Neuron Relationships
The Invariance Property of Orthogonal Transformations
Why Minimizing Hyperspherical Energy is Incorrect for Fine-tuning
Comparison with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA): Structural Differences

outline.description: This chapter details the core contribution of the paper: Orthogonal Finetuning. It walks through the mathematical formulation of applying layer-shared orthogonal matrices to pre-trained weights, ensuring pairwise angles remain invariant while allowing semantic shifts.
subtopics: Mathematical Derivation: Preserving Pairwise Angles via Rotation/Reflection
Initialization Strategies: Starting from Identity Matrices
